newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-ONLY TWO LIKELY TO MISS RE-SCHEDULED NATIONAL.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-ONLY TWO LIKELY TO MISS RE-SCHEDULED NATIONAL.

text.p: Only two horses look like missing Monday's re-scheduled Grand National, leaving 36 runners.
"Everyone is very pleased considering the circumstances," an Aintree spokesman said on Sunday.
Belmont King, who had been quoted at 25-1 is a likely non-runner given the faster ground, and 200-1 complete outsider Over The Stream is also expected to miss the event.

Many of the horses spent the night stabled at nearby Haydock Park racecourse after their ordeal on Saturday when they had to be left for more than two hours during the early part of the security alert which caused the race to be postponed.
An estimated 15 million people gambled about 70 million sterling (112 million dollars) on Saturday's ill-fated event.
David Hill, spokesman for bookmakers William Hill, said "At this time all bets on the race stand. However, bets placed on Saturday on horses that are withdrawn will be refunded."
Bets struck on the course on the Tote have been declared void and money will be returned to punters.
Suny Bay had been among the favourites on Saturday at around 8-1 but on a faster surface may drift a shade in the betting.
Trainer Jenny Pitman, who has twice won the Grand National, saddles her two runners Nahthen Lad and Smith's Band, both 14-1 chances.
She was in tears on Saturday when the horses had to be left on their own. On Sunday she said: "We can't not go on (with the race)."

Charles Barnett, Aintree managing director, said: "Working closely with the police we are going to great lengths to ensure that we stage the big race on Monday. Our staff are sparing no effort in preparing the course and facilities."
The Grand National will be raced on its own with no supporting events.
